l4_steps.name: Analyse crew headcount gap vs. demand forecast
l4_steps.input: 12-month schedule demand forecast, current crew establishment headcount by fleet and base
l4_steps.output: Headcount gap report segmented by fleet type, domicile, and class date window
l4_steps.kpi: Forecast accuracy ±5% vs. actual recruits needed; report delivered ≥10 months ahead of class date
l4_steps.pain_point: Demand forecast volatility from new route announcements and aircraft delivery slippage causes mid-cycle requisition revisions; 9–12-month type-rating lead times mean over/under-hiring is costly and hard to correct

l4_steps.name: Submit and approve crew recruitment requisition
l4_steps.input: Approved headcount gap report, budget allocation from Finance (SAP S/4HANA FI/CO)
l4_steps.output: Approved job requisition record with fleet type, domicile, target class date, and minimum qualifications
l4_steps.kpi: Requisition-to-posting cycle ≤3 business days; budget approval SLA ≤5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP SuccessFactors integration with Jeppesen Crew Management is manual; class date misalignment between HR and Training wastes simulator slots costing $5,000–$12,000 per unused FFS hour

l4_steps.name: Publish vacancy and build candidate pipeline
l4_steps.input: Approved requisition with role minimums (ATP certificate, total flight hours, type rating preferences)
l4_steps.output: Live job posting across channels; ranked candidate pipeline in ATS
l4_steps.kpi: Application-to-qualified-applicant ratio ≥15%; time-to-slate ≤21 days from posting
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR 121.436 ATP minimum (1,500 hours) creates a shallow qualified candidate pool; competition from cargo carriers and regional airlines for experienced pilots drives signing bonus inflation, increasing cost-per-hire beyond budget assumptions

l4_steps.name: Screen applications against FAR 121 ATP minimums
l4_steps.system: SAP SuccessFactors Recruiting + FAA Airmen Inquiry
l4_steps.input: Candidate application submissions; FAA Airmen Inquiry certificate data
l4_steps.output: Shortlisted candidates meeting FAR 121.436 ATP, total hours, and currency requirements
l4_steps.kpi: Screen pass rate ≥40% of qualified applicants; false-negative rate <5% on manual reviews
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual logbook hour verification is time-consuming and fraud-prone; inflated or falsified total-time entries are an industry-wide risk requiring cross-check against FAA Airmen Inquiry — no automated integration exists between ATS and FAA records

l4_steps.name: Conduct HR pre-screen video interview
l4_steps.input: Shortlisted candidate pool from application screening
l4_steps.output: Pre-screen assessment score; advance or decline decision per candidate
l4_steps.kpi: Pre-screen to assessment conversion rate ≥65%; no-show rate <10%
l4_steps.pain_point: Scheduling across time zones for international candidates and active-duty military applicants creates coordination overhead; no-show rates of 10–15% without automated two-way reminder workflows in SuccessFactors deplete pipeline faster than sourcing can replenish

l4_steps.name: Administer aptitude and psychometric assessment
l4_steps.input: Advance decision from pre-screen; candidate email invitation to assessment portal
l4_steps.output: Cognitive aptitude score, personality fit report, and composite recommendation
l4_steps.kpi: Assessment completion rate ≥90%; pass threshold ≥65th percentile on cognitive battery
l4_steps.pain_point: Hogan and Criteria Corp are not natively integrated with SAP SuccessFactors; scores must be manually uploaded, creating data-entry lag and gaps in the EEOC audit trail required for FAR Part 121 carrier compliance

l4_steps.name: Conduct simulator technical assessment — FFS Level D
l4_steps.system: CAE SimuFlite Full-Flight Simulator (FFS Level D)
l4_steps.input: Passed aptitude assessment; confirmed FFS simulator slot from training schedule
l4_steps.output: Simulator assessment gradesheet (pass / conditional / fail) per standardised evaluation form
l4_steps.kpi: First-attempt pass rate ≥75%; FFS simulator utilisation for recruiting ≥80% of booked slots
l4_steps.pain_point: FFS Level D availability is a shared constraint between line training, recurrent training, and recruiting — unplanned FFS maintenance causes candidate rescheduling and downstream class-date delays; recruiting slots are lowest priority in most carriers' FFS allocation policies

l4_steps.name: Conduct structured panel interview and make hire decision
l4_steps.input: FFS gradesheet, aptitude and psychometric scores, pre-screen interview notes
l4_steps.output: Hire or no-hire decision recorded in ATS; offer authorisation initiated
l4_steps.kpi: Offer acceptance rate ≥85%; panel-to-verbal-offer cycle ≤5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Panel scoring without a Behaviourally Anchored Rating Scale (BARS) leads to inconsistent decisions and EEO exposure; calibration sessions between Chief Pilots and HR are ad hoc, creating inter-rater reliability risk that is difficult to defend in EEOC investigations

l4_steps.name: Initiate PRIA check and criminal background screening
l4_steps.system: FAA Airmen Records Clearinghouse (ARC) + HireRight Background Screening
l4_steps.input: Conditional offer accepted; signed PRIA consent form from candidate
l4_steps.output: PRIA report (prior employer records, accident/incident history, drug and alcohol test records); criminal background check result
l4_steps.kpi: PRIA response turnaround ≤30 days (FAR 121.432 statutory deadline); background check completion ≤10 days; disqualification rate <8%
l4_steps.pain_point: FAR 121.432 PRIA requires contacting all prior aviation employers within 5 years — defunct carriers, foreign operators, and unresponsive employers can delay responses by 4–8 weeks with no regulatory enforcement mechanism, directly pushing class dates and increasing training pipeline gaps

l4_steps.name: Schedule and complete FAA Class 1 AME medical exam
l4_steps.system: FAA MedXPress + AME Network (Aviation Medical Examiner)
l4_steps.input: Candidate personal data; completed FAA Form 8500-8 submitted via MedXPress
l4_steps.output: First-Class Medical Certificate issued by AME; MedXPress submission forwarded to FAA AMCD (Aeromedical Certification Division)
l4_steps.kpi: First-class medical pass rate ≥88%; average AME scheduling lead time ≤10 days; medical disqualification identified pre-class ≥95% of cases
l4_steps.pain_point: Candidates with undisclosed conditions (ADHD, cardiovascular history) or special issuance requirements fail at this late stage, creating class fill gaps with no time to backfill; BasicMed provisions do not apply to FAR Part 121 ATP-required operations, so no alternative pathway exists

l4_steps.name: Verify right-to-work and obtain TSA security clearance
l4_steps.system: DHS E-Verify + TSA Security Threat Assessment (STA) Portal
l4_steps.input: Government-issued identity documents; completed I-9 form
l4_steps.output: E-Verify employment authorisation result; TSA STA clearance confirmation number
l4_steps.kpi: E-Verify clearance ≤3 business days; TSA STA clearance ≤21 days; I-9 compliance rate 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: TSA STA delays for candidates with extensive foreign travel history or partial name matches on government watchlists can hold class starts by 2–4 weeks; airline bears DOT liability if any revenue flying occurs before STA clears, requiring costly reallocation of training resources

l4_steps.name: Issue employment contract and confirm class date
l4_steps.input: All compliance checks passed; class date slot confirmed with Training Operations
l4_steps.output: Digitally signed employment contract; new hire record activated in HRIS; class start date confirmed to candidate and training department
l4_steps.kpi: Contract signature to class start ≥14 days buffer; offer-to-class-start cycle ≤90 days; DocuSign completion rate 100% within 3 days of issue
l4_steps.pain_point: Contract terms covering domicile preference, upgrade timelines, and training bond obligations are a primary retention lever — verbal recruiter commitments that diverge from standardised contract language drive year-1 attrition; no single system of record exists to track promises made during recruitment

l4_steps.name: Complete airline indoctrination and systems ground school
l4_steps.system: SAP SuccessFactors Learning (LMS) + Airline CBT Training Portal
l4_steps.input: Class start date; FAR Part 121 Subpart N-approved training syllabus; aircraft systems manuals
l4_steps.output: Ground school completion certificate; aircraft systems knowledge exam result (pass threshold ≥80%)
l4_steps.kpi: Ground school exam first-attempt pass rate ≥90%; dropout or withdrawal rate <5% per class
l4_steps.pain_point: CBT content revision cycles lag behind avionics Service Bulletin (SB) and procedure changes by 6–12 months; new hires learn superseded procedures during ground school and require re-briefing before IOE, increasing Check Airman workload and extending qualification timelines

l4_steps.name: Conduct type rating simulator training under AQP
l4_steps.system: CAE SimuFlite FFS Level D + LOSA Observation Software
l4_steps.input: Ground school completion certificate; FAA-approved Advanced Qualification Programme (AQP) training plan
l4_steps.output: FFS event grades per AQP curriculum; simulator training records logged per FAR 121.409
l4_steps.kpi: FFS training syllabus completion rate 100%; average event grade ≥Satisfactory on all AQP manoeuvres; FFS utilisation ≥85%
l4_steps.pain_point: AQP data management is manual at many carriers — FFS event grades recorded on paper and scanned into training records, creating audit trail gaps for FAA AAIP oversight; LOSA data capture is not standardised, reducing safety data quality for SMS programmes

l4_steps.name: Administer FAA checkride and issue type rating
l4_steps.role: FAA Designated Pilot Examiner (DPE) / AAIP Check Airman
l4_steps.system: FAA IACRA (Integrated Airman Certification and Rating Application)
l4_steps.input: Completed AQP FFS training with all events graded Satisfactory; training records package
l4_steps.output: Temporary airman certificate with type rating endorsement; IACRA application submitted to FAA Registry
l4_steps.kpi: First-attempt checkride pass rate ≥85%; temporary certificate issuance ≤2 days post-exam; permanent certificate ≤120 days per FAA Registry SLA
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA DPE availability is a systemic bottleneck — nationwide DPE shortage means checkride wait times of 2–4 weeks, delaying class graduation and IOE start; airline AAIP (Airline Aviation Training Programme) designation mitigates this but requires dedicated Check Airman capacity that competes with line operations

l4_steps.name: Complete Initial Operating Experience (IOE) line check
l4_steps.role: IOE Check Airman / New Hire First Officer
l4_steps.input: Type rating certificate on file; FAR 121.434 IOE syllabus; assigned IOE pairings in crew schedule
l4_steps.output: IOE completion sign-off by Check Airman; line check gradesheet; FAR 121 line qualification endorsed
l4_steps.kpi: IOE completion within 90 days of type rating issuance (FAR 121.434); first-attempt line check pass rate ≥90%; IOE hours per graduate ≤25 hours
l4_steps.pain_point: IOE pairing availability depends on route and equipment schedule — Jeppesen pairing optimiser does not natively prioritise IOE pairings, causing delays beyond the 90-day FAR 121.434 regulatory window; FAR Part 117 fatigue rules for Check Airmen further constrain IOE scheduling during high operational tempo periods

l4_steps.name: Activate crew qualification record and assign domicile
l4_steps.system: Jeppesen Crew Management + IBS Software iCrew
l4_steps.input: IOE sign-off documentation; type rating on file; employment contract domicile preference
l4_steps.output: Active crew qualification record in Jeppesen; domicile assignment confirmed; PBS eligibility flag set in iCrew
l4_steps.kpi: System activation within 24 hours of IOE sign-off; crew record data accuracy 100%; payroll activation lag ≤1 business day
l4_steps.pain_point: Data synchronisation between Jeppesen crew qualification records and SAP SuccessFactors payroll is manual at most carriers — activation delays cause pay errors and crew portal access failures on day 1 of line flying, generating HR ticket volume and eroding new hire confidence

l4_steps.name: Assign to initial PBS bid period and complete onboarding
l4_steps.role: Crew Planning Analyst / New Hire Pilot
l4_steps.input: Active crew qualification record; open roster positions for current bid period; onboarding task checklist
l4_steps.output: First PBS bid period assignment; completed onboarding compliance tasks (uniform fitting, airport ID, emergency equipment familiarisation, CBA acknowledgement)
l4_steps.kpi: Time from IOE completion to first revenue pairing ≤5 days; onboarding task completion rate 100% by day 30; year-1 voluntary attrition ≤8%
l4_steps.pain_point: New hires unfamiliar with Preferential Bidding System (PBS) mechanics consistently place suboptimal first bids, resulting in undesirable schedules and early attrition complaints; targeted PBS orientation reduces this but is rarely standardised in onboarding programmes, and Jeppesen CrewPlan offers no new-hire guided bidding mode
